$comment: Authored port of the hand-written registry group ecr-policies (docs/plans/compat-coverage-modelgen.md §3.11, G6 wave 3, #1116). The group's only native is the cli suite's (compat/suites/cli/internal/groups/ecr.go); go-sdk, python-sdk, node-js-sdk, java-sdk, dotnet-sdk and rust-sdk never implemented it and carry it as parity debt, which the port closes. It soaked as ecr-policies-shadow beside that native until the nightly comparison (run 36267202659) found none of its 49 (suite, test) pairs diverged in any of three soak runs; the flip then renamed it to ecr-policies, pointed the hand-written registry entry at it and deleted the native code; the clauses are what the native asserted — see compat/model/README.md § Authored scenarios.

groups.$comment: Setup creates the two repositories the native's setup does: `repo`, which carries a lifecycle policy and a repository policy through the group, and `bare`, which never gets a lifecycle policy, so GetLifecyclePolicyNotFound needs no ordering against DeleteLifecyclePolicy. Both are named by $name, so they are {runId}-ecr-policies-repo and -bare: never shared with the native group (whose namer is ecr-pol) or another ECR group, because CreateRepository refuses a repeat and groups run in parallel. Teardown mirrors the native's: the two policies are removed explicitly before the repositories, because the ECR API does not document DeleteRepository as dropping them, then both repositories are deleted with force. The two policy texts are the native's, byte for byte. Every native error check also requires HTTP 400; the IR's error clause has no status, so that half is not carried over — ECR is awsJson1_1 and none of its error shapes names an httpError, so each is the protocol's 400 default. No clause is wrapped in `eventually`: the native reads every write back immediately and polls nothing.
groups.name: ecr-policies

tests.$comment: The native requires the response to echo the policy text exactly and GetLifecyclePolicy to return it exactly. Both are string equality, as in the native, rather than equalsJSON: the native compares bytes, and Overcast stores the text as sent. That the response names the repository is added — the ECR API Reference documents repositoryName in the PutLifecyclePolicy response.
tests.name: PutLifecyclePolicy

tests.$comment: The native's two checks: the stored text, and the repository it belongs to.
tests.name: GetLifecyclePolicy

tests.$comment: The native requires the response to name the repository and GetLifecyclePolicy then to raise LifecyclePolicyNotFoundException (its HTTP 400 is not carried; see the group). The API Reference also documents lifecyclePolicyText in this response, which Overcast omits; the native never read it, so it is not asserted here.
tests.name: DeleteLifecyclePolicy

tests.$comment: GetLifecyclePolicy on the repository that never had one: LifecyclePolicyNotFoundException, as the native requires (its HTTP 400 is not carried; see the group). No depends, as in the registry.
tests.name: GetLifecyclePolicyNotFound

tests.$comment: The native requires the response to echo the policy text exactly and GetRepositoryPolicy to return it exactly — string equality, as in the native. AWS may re-serialize a repository policy it stores; the native asserts the bytes, and so does the port, so a later move to equalsJSON is a decision to make against AWS rather than one to make silently here. That the response names the repository is added — the ECR API Reference documents repositoryName in the SetRepositoryPolicy response.
tests.name: SetRepositoryPolicy

tests.$comment: The native's two checks: the stored text, and the repository it belongs to.
tests.name: GetRepositoryPolicy

tests.$comment: The native requires the response to name the repository and GetRepositoryPolicy then to raise RepositoryPolicyNotFoundException (its HTTP 400 is not carried; see the group). The API Reference also documents policyText in this response, which Overcast omits; the native never read it, so it is not asserted here.
tests.name: DeleteRepositoryPolicy
